office_does: The Assessor sets the market value of all real and personal property in the county, the base used to calculate property taxes; the Assessor does not set tax rates.
race_blurb: Two candidates who both prefer the Democratic Party are running for the open seat. JJ Olson, a decade-long appraiser in the office endorsed by outgoing Assessor Steven Drew, led the primary 55% to 42% over Lynda Nashed Zeman, a county executive administrator and former appointed Lacey councilmember.

candidates.summary: Business Applications Administrator in the Assessor's Office and accredited appraiser who started as a field appraiser about ten years ago; endorsed by the outgoing Assessor and office staff.
highlights: Accredited Washington real property appraiser since 2016; started as a field appraiser and now manages the office's appraisal and tax software [S1]
Says he is leading a technology transformation to make the office more accessible and transparent [S1]
Promises plain-language explanations of how property values are set [S2]
Endorsed by Assessor Steven Drew, 20 current and former office staff, the regional labor council and the county REALTORS association [S3]
Led the certified August primary with 55.10% of the vote [S5]

experience.basis: Continuity candidate: about a decade inside the Assessor's Office, endorsed by the outgoing incumbent and chief deputy; no elected record.

candidates.summary: Executive administrator in the County Commissioners' Office who previously did executive administration in the Assessor's Office for three years; appointed Lacey City Councilmember in 2019.
highlights: Frames the Assessor's job as executive leadership over people, budgets and systems [S1]
Names staff retirements, growing workloads, tight budgets and the systems transition as the office's main challenges [S1]
Would make valuation information easier to understand so owners get answers "before frustration turns into appeals" [S1]
Vice president of the West Puget Sound chapter of the International Association of Assessing Officers [S2]
Endorsed by 22nd LD legislators, two county commissioners and the mayors of Olympia, Tumwater, Yelm and Tenino [S2]

experience.basis: Mixed profile: a county-government insider with a 2019 council appointment, but not the office's continuity pick, running on management change rather than appraisal tenure.

spending.basis: Pledges to "manage resources responsibly" under tight budgets and to run the office with fiscal responsibility; no specific spending proposals.
